source._smooth_window_doc: 2026-11-01 (ledger 0060, High Plains' lesson): source/osm_oval_fixes.json is a list of 63 OSM nodes (5.6 m apart in the turns, up to 119 m on the straights), not a 1 Hz GPS drive; from_track's 5-fix moving average put the line 2.67 m median / 3.30 p95 / 3.69 m max off the source polygon. 0 = no smoothing: the line is the OSM polygon resampled at 3 m (build_mesh still corner-rounds it for the sweep). The closing 119 m (last node -> first) is a straight's own segment (0.0 deg turn at both ends), not a chord.
source._note: Re-sourced from real OSM highway=raceway way 1134026181 at Fountain, CO (reversed to CW winding), resampled to 3 m via scripts.gps.from_track. Real 1.03-mi D-oval; elevation from USGS 3DEP (real ~2 m sunken bowl, do not flatten).

road_profile._doc: 1.65 km paved oval/roval, engineered and near-flat. 3DEP sampled every 3 m over a lap this short is mostly DEM surface noise, and the 33 m default median cannot reject it: 130-236 kinks/km against a 3%-slope-change threshold, i.e. a jagged deck everywhere rather than a few bad spots. Same lever that fixed Second Creek. A graded racetrack is smooth by construction; the profile should be too.
road_profile._ribbon_cols_doc: 2026-11-01: 8 lateral columns so the bank ramps' twist doesn't sag the deck between 3 m rows (ribbon.road_ribbon cols; absent = one edge-to-edge quad), Exotics' value: its v0.1.0 drive_test read 28 severe steps of up to 13 cm, all in its camber ramps, and the chain build with 8 cols (and 85 m ramps for its old 20 m) read 0. Here ledger 0018's V1 severe-step clusters (10 at s 240, 11 at s 640, 10 at s 1020, 12 at s 1400, on a 1,649 m lap) sit on the four ramps of the V1 arcs (231-281, 616-666, 1007-1057, 1392-1442) — if those arcs were in that build (dated 2026-07-20 in route._orientation_doc; the rewritten history cannot confirm the order here). A 15 m deck rolling 0 -> 10 deg over 50 m is the twist this column count exists for. Not a gate change; the Windows run's drive_test says whether it was the mechanism.

road_profile._arcs_doc: 2026-11-01: what the two arcs cover. L10: PPIR is banked 10 deg in all four turns. A 1-mile oval's four turns are its two ends: T1-T2 is one continuous left-hand end, T3-T4 the other, so one arc per end, each covering two turns. Windows from the curvature of this config's own line (smooth_window 0, reversed, rotated to start_at; curvature over +/-15 m): T1-T2 turns in at s ~230 (2.2 -> 5.1 /km at s 210 -> 240) and out at s ~705 (4.7 -> 0.9 /km at s 690 -> 720), min R 118 m; T3-T4 in at s ~985 (0.0 -> 3.2 /km at s 960 -> 990, the back stretch dead straight 720-960) and out at s ~1475 (3.2 -> 1.9 /km at s 1470 -> 1500), min R 123 m. Each 50 m raised-cosine ramp is centred on the turn-in / turn-out, so full bank holds from s 265 to 680 and from 1010 to 1450. The V1 arcs (231 + 435, 1007 + 435) were cut on the smoothed line, 17 m shorter, and ended 40-60 m before the turns did. The straights stay flat: the front stretch's dogleg (~2 /km, R ~500 m, s 1500-230 across the start) and the back stretch carry no researched banking, and L10 says do not invent it. bank_deg is NEGATIVE: profile.py's +ve banks a right-hander (left edge up) in the chain's unmirrored frame; every PPIR turn is a left-hander (raced counterclockwise), so its outside, raised edge is the RIGHT one. Check on the built deck: the raised edge must be the outside (the one farther from the infield). 2026-11-03, 0.4.0 (ledger 0077): the lidar survey (source/lidar/camber-survey) measured what the research lacked. The straights are banked too (front dogleg ~7.2 deg, back stretch ~3.0 deg), and the rolls run over 130-165 m, not 50. So the cambers are five plateau windows whose 150 m ramps coincide, each entry with its _source: researched + measured, plateaus and ramps only (L10), not the per-station profile.

route._orientation_doc: Research 2026-07-20: PPIR oval raced COUNTERCLOCKWISE (NASCAR/IRL 1997-2005); S/F mid front stretch in front of the main grandstand (~38.5910,-104.6785), cars heading SSE. Our OSM ring was CW -> route.reverse. Cambers re-derived from curvature after reversal; bank sign flipped (+10) because outside/inside swap when direction reverses — verify outside-edge-up in Blender/game.

edge._doc: the circuit edge (ledger 0078): no curb, no sidewalk. The asphalt edge is held at road height for 0.30 m and the run-off ground meets it 0.15 m lower over 1.0 m [invented: the flush meet the drive gate reads as no drop]; the ground beyond is the assembler's conform to the road, then the 3DEP surface: the real run-off level.
